operator_evidence: AAR Appendix A: NORDUnet interface flapping reported at 15:33 (INC0040272); customer disabled the interface at 16:50 to regain stability; availability window 16:50-21:33 (INC0040289); interface re-enabled at 20:48.
bgp_observation: 11 of 33 selected observer-prefix streams (all AS2603 via AS11537) became absent at 16:45:25Z and returned at 16:45:27Z (2 s); 30 path replacements followed (16:45:26-17:02:03Z), with 11 streams departing the reviewed transit and 11 retaining it with material path changes; all 33 streams returned to baseline paths by 17:02:19Z.
temporal_relationship: Before / within stated precision (absence 16:45:25Z; reported disable 16:50 UTC)
interpretation: Temporally consistent with an exported routing consequence of the reported instability and interface disable; public BGP does not reveal the interface command, and temporal consistency does not prove causation.
limitation: One selected public collector (route-views2, single peer 64.57.28.241); a 2-second absence at one observer may reflect session behavior rather than the participant's own action; Layer-2 replication and the interface command are not observable in public BGP.
finding: Public BGP exposed a temporally related routing consequence for one reviewed participant (NORDUnet, AS2603) at one selected public collector during the reported incident. This is a single-target, single-collector, single-window pilot — it is not a complete MAN LAN incident verdict.
